title: Annotation compactness and noise playbook (personal worklog)
content:
Notes to self / working playbook for small-but-frequent label noise patterns (compactness = how tightly we group tokens into a single label).

Overview:
- Problem space: lots of soft disagreements around whether to split or merge adjacent tokens into a single span (names + titles, currency + amounts, code fragments, hyphenated terms, id-like tokens). These affect model recall heavily when inconsistent.
- Goal: lightweight heuristics labelers can apply quickly, plus a small audit script to catch regressions. Keep rules permissive but consistent.

Quick heuristics (tip sheet):
1) Titles + name ("Dr. Amy Lee", "Prof John Smith"):
   - Prefer single PERSON span if title is inseparable in downstream apps (e.g., persona extraction).
   - If title is functional metadata ("CEO Amy Lee") consider two spans: ROLE and PERSON.
   - If unsure, mark single PERSON and add note in comment.

2) Currency + amount: always merge into single MONEY span if currency symbol present adjacent ("$45", "€ 3.50").
   - If written words ("forty five dollars") prefer single MONEY.

3) Hyphenated tokens ("state-of-the-art", "x-ray"):
   - If hyphenated phrase is lexicalized (freq in English > 1000 in our corpus) -> single TERM span.
   - Otherwise, prefer split spans per token and annotate relationship in comments if needed.

4) IDs and short alphanumerics ("AB-1234", "usr_007"):
   - Treat as single IDENTIFIER span. If scheme is ambiguous, tag as IDENTIFIER and leave notes.

5) Embedded code snippets inline ("printf(\"hi\")"):
   - Label entire snippet as CODE. If function names inside are important as entities, create inner spans only when explicitly requested by label spec. Generally keep compact.

6) Dates/time ranges:
   - Adjacent tokens that together represent a single temporal expression -> single DATE span ("Aug 3-5, 2024").

7) Nested spans (company + product):
   - Prefer outer COMPANY and inner PRODUCT only when product is marketed separately. If ambiguous, favor single ORGANIZATION span to reduce noise.

Ambiguity examples + gold decision (for quick reference):
- "Apple store" -> ORGANIZATION (single).
- "Apple Watch" -> PRODUCT (single).
- "Dr. Jane Kumar" -> PERSON (include title if downstream requires).
- "invoice # 2321" -> IDENTIFIER (merge prefix + number).
- "3/4" -> if seen in math context -> MATH; otherwise DATE/UNKNOWN -> add comment.

Micro-audit checks (to run weekly):
- Rule A: Find tokens where some examples have adjacent-span vs split-span for same canonical form. Sample 200 examples, flag if >10% disagreement.
- Rule B: Detect mixed-case short IDs sometimes labeled as words; look for patterns like [A-Z]{2,}-\d{3,} labeled as WORD.
- Rule C: Currency seen as two spans vs one -> sample and standardize.

Lightweight regexes I keep using (notes to self):
- ID-ish: "\b[A-Z]{2,}-?\d{2,,}\b"
- Currency symbol adjacency: "(\$|€|£)\s?\d"
- Hyphenated words: "\b\w+(?:-\w+)+\b"
- Inline code heur: "`[^`]+`|\\b[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*\\(.*?\\)"

Example before/after (for labeler training snippets):
- raw: "Dr. Salim will invoice $450 for X-ray services on 2025-12-01."
  labels: PERSON=[Dr. Salim]; MONEY=[$450]; SERVICE=[X-ray services]; DATE=[2025-12-01]

- raw: "Use inv-4321 when contacting ops."
  labels: IDENTIFIER=[inv-4321]; ROLE=[ops] (if ops is team name, else leave text)

Edge case catalog (short):
- multi-lingual punctuation (non-breaking spaces around currency, arabic digits mixed with western numerals) -> add normalization step before labeling pipeline.
- zero-width joiners in names -> strip for matching but preserve in final text.
- contractions with punctuation ("U.S.-based") -> treat as single LOCATION/ORG if common token.

Open questions / TODOs: (for discussion with Priya/Liam)
- Should "title + name" be configurable per dataset? e.g., legal docs vs chat transcripts have different needs. (RFC?)
- Add an optional label "COMPACT_DECISION" for borderline labels so downstream can learn noise patterns.
- Prioritize building an "auto-suggest" sanitization pipeline using the regexes above; POC script in PR #78 but needs perf testing.

Quick POC audit command (pseudo):
- python scripts/audit_compactness.py --sample 1000 --threshold 0.1 --out report.csv
- heuristics: compare span token count distributions grouped by canonical token form. Flag forms with both 1-token and multi-token > threshold.

Notes from last sync:
- Liam: wants a PR to add ID regex to labeling UI autocomplete (https://github.com/redwood-inference/data-labeling/pull/78).
- Priya: suggested a small training module for raters: "3 minute rules" card — we should have 6 example pairs for each rule.

Mini action plan (next 2 weeks):
- [ ] Draft 6 quick example pairs for titles, currency, hyphenation, ids, code, dates. (Maya)
- [ ] Add regex-based normalizer to labeling pipeline and run against 100k rows. (Liam)
- [ ] Create short rater quiz in Labelbox for fast quality check; target pass rate 85%. (Priya)
- [ ] Ship small audit script and add CI hook to daily job. (follow-up in RDC-987)

Random brain dump:
- Might be worth a small ML model to predict "compactness preference" (binary: merge vs split) trained on already-labeled pairs — could reduce rater friction. Keep this low-priority.

References / bookmarks:
- RDC-987 — labeling compactness audit (Jira)
- PR #78 — normalizer + regex patches
- Slack thread "label-compactness" for recent rater examples

If I revisit: convert top heuristics into a 1-page cheat sheet and pin on the labeling board. Keep this doc as the lab notebook for experiments and odd examples.

End of worklog entry.
